notes: The extension docs (docs/extensions/toc.md) don't mention the `no-toc` class, which is the place users would look for it. Consider adding a short section next to the `data-toc-label` docs.
The class name is hard-coded. The issue says a configurable name is optional, so this is acceptable.

Without the code change, the new tests would fail: test_ac_fr_001_1_hrefs asserts that href="#contents" is missing. I could not re-run them against the base code because git operations are blocked in this environment.
When a no-toc heading has children, they move up to the previous ancestor in the TOC (e.g. h3 Child appears under h1 A). This is reasonable but not documented.
summary: The PR adds one condition to TocTreeprocessor: headings whose class list contains `no-toc` are left out of toc_tokens, and therefore out of md.toc and the [TOC] output. They still get their id and permalink. I ran the issue's example and two edge cases (a similar class name, an excluded heading with children), and all behaved correctly. The full suite passes and the changelog entry is present. The change stays inside the toc extension and doesn't violate ARCHITECTURE.md. The only gap is missing user docs in docs/extensions/toc.md, which doesn't block merging.
